708269.t: From Proto-Hellenic *lúkos, from Proto-Indo-European *wĺ̥kʷos (“wolf”) with metathesis. Cognates include Sanskrit वृक (vṛ́ka), Latin lupus (also showing metathesis), Old English wulf (English wolf) and Russian волк (volk).

708236.t: From Proto-Hellenic *lógos, from Proto-Indo-European *leǵ- (“to collect (words)”). See also λέγω (légō, “to reckon, say”).

708234.t: From λογίζομαι (logízomai, “I calculate”) + -μός (-mós, verbal noun suffix).

708288.t: From Proto-Indo-European *lewh₁- (“to cut off, separate, free”) (which Beekes reconstructs as *lh₁u-).

708232.t: From λόγος (lógos, “computation, reckoning”) + -ίζομαι (-ĭ́zomai, denominative mediopassive verb suffix).

708237.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂k- (“to hit”), compare Latin lancea (“lance”) and Old Armenian գեղարդն (gełardn, “spear”), or a Semitic borrowing corresponding to Hebrew רֹמַח (rómaḥ, “spear”), Arabic رُمْح (rumḥ, “spear”) etc. (see the Arabic),…

708261.t: O-grade verbal noun from λέχομαι (lékhomai, “to lie”). Cognate with Albanian lagje.

708208.t: A zero-grade formation from or closely related to λιμήν (limḗn, “harbor”) and λειμών (leimṓn, “moist place, meadow”).

708210.t: Uncertain, though probably connected to and from the same family of words as λοιμός (loimós, “plague”).

708213.t: Uncertain. First attested as Mycenaean Greek 𐀪𐀜 (ri-no), could be from Proto-Indo-European *linom, with cognates including Old Church Slavonic льнъ (lĭnŭ), Latin līnum, and Gothic 𐌻𐌴𐌹𐌽 (lein).

708202.t: From Proto-Indo-European *neyk-. Cognates include Lithuanian niekoti, Latvian niekāt, and Welsh nithio.

708258.t: From Proto-Indo-European *lewh₃- (“to wash; to bathe”). Cognates include Albanian laj, Latin lavō, Old Armenian լոգանամ (loganam), and Old English lēaþor (English lather).

708229.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *leb- Proto-Indo-European *-os Proto-Indo-European *-ós Proto-Indo-European *-ós Proto-Indo-European *lobós Proto-Hellenic *lobós? Ancient Greek λοβός Uncertain, though perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“to hang…

708245.t: Of uncertain origin, though perhaps related to λιμός (līmós, “famine”) (via ablaut), as well as λοιγός (loigós, “ruin”) (via different suffix). Compare λύμη (lū́mē), λῦμα (lûmă), λυμαίνομαι (lūmaínomai)

708248.t: From Proto-Indo-European *loykʷós (“remaining, leftover”). Surface analysis λείπω (leípō, “to leave, remain”) + -ός (-ós, deverbal adjective suffix).

708240.t: Taken as a formation comparable to πολιορκέω (polĭorkéō), δειροτομέω (deirotoméō), οἰνοχέω (oinokhéō), but further details are unknown.

708295.t: Uncertain. Possibly inherited from Proto-Indo-European *me (“by, close/close to, near/near to”, adverb).

708257.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *lewotrón, whence also Mycenaean Greek 𐀩𐀺𐀵𐀫 (re-wo-to-ro /⁠lewotrón⁠/), from Proto-Indo-European *léwh₃trom (“that which is used for washing”), from *lewh₃- (“to wash, bathe”); see there for further cognates.

708207.t: Ablaut derivation from Proto-Indo-European *léymō (“lake”); compare λίμνη (límnē). See λειμών (leimṓn) for a descendant in a different ablaut grade.

708291.t: Maybe from Proto-Indo-European *h₂welh₁- (“hair, wool”), like Latin vellus (“fleece”), or from the same root of Ancient Greek εὔληρα (eúlēra, “rein”), Latin lōrum (“thong”) and Old Armenian լար (lar, “rope”).

708219.t: From the same root as λιτός (lĭtós, “supplicatory”) and λιτή (lĭtḗ, “prayer, entreaty”), said root of unknown origin, but the fact that the λ (l) often makes a preceding short vowel into a heavy syllable, as well as the frequent doubling of the λ (l) after…

708224.t: From Proto-Indo-European *leyb-, the same root as λείβω (leíbō, “to pour”).

708256.t: By surface analysis, λούω (loúō, “to wash, bathe”) + -τήρ (-tḗr). Compare λουτρόν (loutrón, “bathing-place”).

708281.t: From λύω (lúō, “to set free, release”) + -τρον (-tron, “a suffix forming instrument nouns”).

708274.t: From λυπέω (lūpéō, “to grieve”) + -ρός (-rós). Compare also λυπρός (lūprós).

708280.t: From λυσι- (lusi-, “loosing, releasing”), from λύω (lúō) + -τελής (-telḗs), from τέλος (télos, “end, completion; here: dues”).

708284.t: From λυτρόω (lutróō, “to ransom”) + -σις (-sis, “a suffix added to verb stems to form abstract nouns or nouns of action, result or process”)

708285.t: From λυτρόω (lutróō, “to ransom”) + -τής (-tḗs, “a suffix forming agent nouns”)

708209.t: From λιμός (limós) + κτείνω (kteínō), equivalent to λιμοκτόνος (limoktónos) + -έω (-éō).
